blog_summary: OmniLedger is presented as a groundbreaking decentralized ledger system that achieves Visa-level scalability while maintaining security and permissionless decentralization. Adrian Colyer highlights OmniLedger as a notable advancement in distributed systems and transaction processing, emphasizing its innovative combination of standard building blocks like sharding, Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT), and secure randomness generation. The paper introduces novel protocols such as Omnicon for intra-shard consensus and Atomix for secure cross-shard transactions, demonstrating how these components work together to enable linear scalability and low latency. The blog post also underscores the rapid progress in decentralized ledgers, positioning OmniLedger as a wake-up call for researchers in distributed systems who may have overlooked developments in this area. Key insights include the use of an identity blockchain, RandHound for secure randomness, and cryptographic sortition for leader election, all of which contribute to the system's robustness and security.
paper_title: OmniLedger: A secure, scale-out, decentralized ledger via sharding
paper_abstract: —Designing a secure permissionless distributed ledger (blockchain) that performs on par with centralized payment processors, such as Visa, is a challenging task. Most existing distributed ledgers are unable to scale-out, i.e., to grow their total processing capacity with the number of validators; and those that do, compromise security or decentralization. We present OmniLedger, a novel scale-out distributed ledger that preserves longterm security under permissionless operation. It ensures security and correctness by using a bias-resistant public-randomness protocol for choosing large, statistically representative shards that process transactions, and by introducing an efficient crossshard commit protocol that atomically handles transactions affecting multiple shards. OmniLedger also optimizes performance via parallel intra-shard transaction processing, ledger pruning via collectively-signed state blocks, and low-latency “trust-butverify” validation for low-value transactions. An evaluation of our experimental prototype shows that OmniLedger’s throughput scales linearly in the number of active validators, supporting Visa-level workloads and beyond, while confirming typical transactions in under two seconds.
